NDT training in New Orleans: how it works for New Orleans employers and technicians

Short answer: NDT training for New Orleans is delivered live online or onsite at your own plant, yard or shop. Atlantis NDT has no classroom in the city. An ASNT NDT Level III runs Level I, II and III courses in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A, then helps your company examine and certify technicians under its own written practice. Cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day.

That short answer hides the part most people searching for NDT classes in New Orleans have not been told: in the United States nobody hands you a national NDT licence. Under SNT-TC-1A your employer certifies you, against a written practice that its Level III signs. Training is one ingredient. The others are documented on-the-job experience, three examinations (general, specific and practical), a vision test and the employer's signature. A course certificate from any provider, including us, is evidence of training hours. It is not, on its own, permission to perform and interpret inspections.

For a New Orleans contractor, the useful question is therefore not where to find a class but how to move a crew through the whole chain (hours, experience, examinations, paperwork) before the next turnaround at a River Parishes refinery or the next vessel comes onto a West Bank dry dock. For an individual, it means lining up an employer, or a realistic route to one, early, because the experience clock only runs while you are working in the method under certified supervision.

We work with both groups. Employers get onsite or live-virtual cohorts, Level III examination support and written-practice work. Individuals can join live online theory and prepare for employer examinations, while the practical examination is always carried out on real specimens in front of a qualified examiner. Request a New Orleans training quote with the methods, levels and head-count you have in mind.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in New Orleans

Every course below is built on the SNT-TC-1A body of knowledge for the method and taught by or under an ASNT NDT Level III. What changes from city to city is the emphasis: which product forms, which codes and which acceptance criteria the practical exercises lean on. For New Orleans that means process piping and vessels in the refinery and chemical corridor, structural and hull steel in the marine yards, and pipeline girth welds feeding the terminals.

MethodLevelsWhat New Orleans employers use it forPrerequisite
UT (ultrasonic testing)I, II, IIIThickness surveys on process piping and vessels during River Parishes turnarounds; shear-wave weld examination on new-construction piping; hull and tank plate gauging in the marine yardsLevel I: the education and experience entry rules in your written practice. Level II: Level I plus documented method experience
PAUT (phased array UT)II, IIIWeld examination on petrochemical and LNG new construction where the code and owner allow UT in place of RT; corrosion mapping of elbows and nozzlesConventional UT Level II strongly recommended first
TOFD (time-of-flight diffraction)II, IIIHeavy-wall vessel and column seam welds in fabrication shops; height sizing of planar flaws found during turnaroundsUT Level II
RT (radiographic testing)I, II, IIIPipe welds in fabrication shops and pipeline tie-ins, vessel seams, film and digital image interpretationAnyone handling sources also needs Louisiana radiographer certification (separate from NDT certification)
MT (magnetic particle)I, IIStructural welds on offshore modules, crane pedestals, lifting gear and fatigue-sensitive hull detailsNone beyond written-practice entry rules
PT (liquid penetrant)I, IIStainless and nickel-alloy piping in chemical plants, machined non-magnetic parts, weld prep and back-gouge checksNone beyond written-practice entry rules
VT (visual testing)I, IIWeld visual on every job, fit-up and root checks, coating and corrosion condition surveys on tanks and structuresNone beyond written-practice entry rules
ET (eddy current)I, II, IIIHeat-exchanger and condenser tube inspection during turnarounds and power-plant outages; surface crack detection through coatingsNone; prior UT or MT experience helps

UT Level I and II. The course runs from sound physics and transducer selection to calibration on reference blocks, straight-beam thickness work, angle-beam weld scanning and reporting. For New Orleans cohorts the practical exercises weight corrosion surveys on piping with insulation removed, because that is where much of the region's UT volume sits: coastal humidity and salt air make corrosion under insulation a constant finding, and owners often shorten survey intervals in response to measured corrosion rates. Angle-beam work covers the ASME Section V techniques that fabrication shops and owner specifications in the corridor refer to. See UT Level 2 practice questions for a sense of how the general examination is pitched.

PAUT and TOFD. These are Level II and III courses for technicians who already hold conventional UT. They cover focal laws, sectorial and linear scans, encoded scanning, setup files, flaw sizing and data review. On the Louisiana side of the Gulf Coast, advanced UT demand comes from two directions: new construction where an owner has accepted UT in place of radiography to keep crews working around the clock without radiation barricades, and in-service corrosion mapping where a grid of manual thickness readings would miss localised loss.

RT Level I and II. The course covers radiation physics, exposure calculation, film and digital techniques, image quality indicators, and above all interpretation: telling slag from porosity from lack of fusion on real radiographs. Interpretation is what employers here pay for. The course is not a radiation-safety licence; handling Ir-192 or Se-75 sources in Louisiana is controlled separately by the state (see below).

MT, PT and VT. These are the workhorse methods in the marine and structural yards, and they are often the first certifications a new technician earns. Courses cover magnetisation technique, yoke and prod work, wet and dry particles, penetrant process control, dwell and developer, and the visual acuity and lighting conditions the examination depends on. VT training includes weld profile, undercut and reinforcement gauging against common acceptance criteria.

ET. Eddy current training covers impedance-plane interpretation, probe selection and calibration, with the practical steered toward tubing (bobbin probes on heat-exchanger bundles) or surface work, depending on what your crew does. Turnaround exchanger work is steady demand in the corridor.

Level III. For technicians and supervisors aiming at Level III, we run preparation for the ASNT Basic and Method examinations and cover procedure writing, which is the skill that matters once you hold the certificate. See ASNT Level III training.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in New Orleans, step by step

  1. Your employer adopts a written practice. This controlled document, based on SNT-TC-1A, sets the training hours, experience hours, examination content, passing grades, vision requirements and recertification interval for each method and level. If your company does not have one, that is step zero (see the Level III section below).
  2. Classroom training. You complete the formal training hours your written practice sets for the method and level, live online, onsite or blended. The training-requirements matrix shows the SNT-TC-1A recommended figures by method and level; your written practice can require more.
  3. On-the-job experience. You log hours performing the method under a certified Level II or Level III. This is usually the slowest part and cannot be done in a classroom or a simulator.
  4. General examination. A written test on the method's principles, equipment and terminology.
  5. Specific examination. A written test on your employer's procedures, equipment, codes and acceptance criteria. For a New Orleans refinery contractor this might mean API-referenced thickness procedures and B31.3 acceptance; for a yard it might mean ABS or AWS D1.1 criteria.
  6. Practical examination. You demonstrate the method on real specimens with known discontinuities, write the report and have it graded by a Level III or a qualified examiner working under one.
  7. Vision examination. A near-vision acuity test and a colour-contrast check, repeated at the interval your written practice sets (near vision is at least annual under SNT-TC-1A).
  8. Certification. Your employer's certifying authority signs the certification record. It is valid while you work for that employer and within the stated period.
  9. Recertification. At the interval in the written practice (SNT-TC-1A recommends no more than five years), you are recertified by examination or by documented continuing performance, as the written practice allows.

More detail on how the pieces fit together is on our SNT-TC-1A training and certification page.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for New Orleans crews

We are specific about delivery because it matters for scheduling. There are three ways we run training for New Orleans:

  • Live online classes. Instructor-led sessions in real time, not recorded slides, covering the theory portion of Level I and II courses and Level III preparation. Useful for technicians rotating between sites in St. Charles, St. John and St. James parishes, and for individuals who cannot leave work for a week. See online NDT training.
  • Onsite at your facility. An ASNT Level III-led team comes to your plant, shop or yard, teaches on your equipment and examines on specimens that look like your work. This is how most employer cohorts run. See corporate NDT training.
  • Blended. Theory online, then a concentrated practical block onsite with examinations. This suits contractors who cannot pull a whole crew off rotation at once.

Timing is the part local employers care about most. Refinery and chemical turnarounds along the river cluster in the spring and autumn, and the Atlantic hurricane season runs from June through November, which both disrupts schedules and creates urgent post-storm inspection work. The best windows for onsite training are usually the weeks just before a turnaround (so certificates are in hand when the gate opens) or quieter periods between campaigns. Tell us your outage and campaign calendar and we will build around it. Ask about onsite training for your New Orleans crew.

One honest limit: practical examinations cannot be done remotely. Whatever the delivery mode, the practical is done hands-on, with real equipment on real specimens.

Where NDT technicians work in New Orleans

The New Orleans metro is an unusual NDT market because several very different asset owners sit within an hour's drive, and each brings its own codes and gate requirements.

Refining and chemicals along the Mississippi. The corridor starts in the city's own backyard, with refineries in St. Bernard Parish at Chalmette and Meraux, and continues upriver through the Norco and St. Charles Parish complexes, the chemical plants around Hahnville and Taft, and the large refinery at Garyville in St. John the Baptist Parish, on toward Baton Rouge. Inspection here is driven by in-service codes: API 510 for vessels, API 570 for piping and API 653 for tanks. Owner inspectors often hold API individual certifications, and many employers also ask for them, but the NDT itself is performed by method-certified technicians. New construction and repairs run to ASME Section VIII and B31.3, with methods defined in ASME Section V.

Marine, offshore and port work. The Port of New Orleans, the West Bank yards and the offshore support bases toward Houma and Port Fourchon generate MT, UT gauging and VT on hulls, deck machinery, cranes and offshore modules. Classification society (ABS) and U.S. Coast Guard survey requirements set the acceptance side, and AWS D1.1 governs much of the structural fabrication.

Pipelines and terminals. Crude, product and gas lines crossing south Louisiana feed terminals, the Louisiana Offshore Oil Port and export facilities. Girth-weld radiography and increasingly automated UT on new lines follow API 1104, with PHMSA rules under 49 CFR Parts 192 and 195 behind the operators.

Power and nuclear. Entergy's Waterford 3 nuclear plant at Killona in St. Charles Parish runs outages that pull in outage-support NDT, and nuclear in-service inspection follows ASME Section XI. Be clear-eyed: nuclear UT often requires performance demonstration qualification that sits on top of SNT-TC-1A training, and utilities set their own access requirements.

Aerospace and heavy manufacturing. NASA's Michoud Assembly Facility in New Orleans East builds large launch-vehicle structures, and the tenants and suppliers around it work to aerospace specifications. Some of those employers also ask for NAS 410 qualification, which is a different scheme; our training is SNT-TC-1A-based.

Bridges and public works. The Crescent City Connection, the Huey P. Long Bridge and the long causeway and trestle structures around Lake Pontchartrain are steel and concrete assets that owners inspect on cycles. Bridge weld work typically follows AWS D1.5.

Radiography licensing in Louisiana. Louisiana is an NRC Agreement State, and the Louisiana Department of Environmental Quality (LDEQ) regulates radioactive material and radiation-producing machines under LAC 33:XV. LDEQ itself certifies industrial radiographers, trainees and instructors, and anyone performing industrial radiography with sources or X-ray equipment in the state must hold that certification. Out-of-state companies working in Louisiana use LDEQ's reciprocity process. This radiation-safety certification is completely separate from SNT-TC-1A certification in RT: a New Orleans radiographer typically needs both, one for the right to handle the source safely and one for the competence to take and interpret the image.

What employers here typically ask for at the gate. A current method certification under the contractor's written practice, the written practice itself on file, training and experience records, a current vision record, site safety orientations, a TWIC card for port and maritime facilities, and for RT the LDEQ radiographer card. Salary expectations vary widely by method and sector; our NDT salary guide summarises public sources rather than quoting local figures we cannot verify.

Level III services and written practices for New Orleans NDT companies

Many small and mid-sized inspection companies in the metro, including crews spun out of larger contractors, run without a full-time Level III. That works until a refinery QA auditor asks for the written practice, the examination records and the Level III's credentials, and the file is thin. We help in three ways:

  • Written practice development or review. We write or audit your SNT-TC-1A written practice so it matches the methods you actually perform and the codes your clients cite. See written practice development.
  • Examination administration. General, specific and practical examinations prepared and graded under ASNT Level III oversight, with records filed the way auditors expect.
  • Procedure writing and technique approval. Method procedures aligned to ASME Section V, API 1104, AWS D1.1 or client specifications, reviewed by a Level III.

This is the same framework described on our SNT-TC-1A guidance page. Book a Level III consultation if your written practice is overdue for review or you are bidding work that asks for one.

Practise before the practical exam

The Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees practise 12 NDT methods in 5 virtual environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. For New Orleans trainees, the oil and gas site and storage tank scenes are the closest match to corridor work, and the welding workshop suits yard and fabrication crews. It is a place to rehearse setups, scanning patterns and decision-making between classes. It is practice only: it does not replace hands-on training time, logged experience or the practical examination on real specimens.

Your instructor

Courses are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He sets the course content, oversees examinations and reviews written practices and procedures for employer clients.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in New Orleans

How do I get NDT certified in New Orleans?

Get hired by, or sponsored by, an employer that works under an SNT-TC-1A written practice; complete the classroom training hours for your method and level; log supervised on-the-job experience; pass the general, specific and practical examinations and the vision test; then your employer certifies you. We provide the training, exam preparation and Level III support in that chain, online or at your employer's site.

Can I take NDT training online in Louisiana?

Yes, for theory. Live online classes cover the classroom portion of Level I and II courses and Level III preparation. The practical training and practical examination must be hands-on, which is why we pair online theory with onsite practical blocks for employers.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on your written practice. SNT-TC-1A recommends minimum classroom hours and experience hours for UT Level I and Level II, and experience is usually the constraint, not class time. Check the training-requirements matrix for the recommended figures, then count what you already have logged.

Do I need a license for radiography in Louisiana?

Yes. Anyone performing industrial radiography in Louisiana needs an industrial radiographer certification issued by LDEQ, and the company needs an LDEQ radioactive material licence or machine registration. That is separate from SNT-TC-1A RT certification, which covers technique and interpretation competence.

What does NDT training cost in New Orleans?

We do not publish prices, because cost depends on the method, the level, group size, whether delivery is online or onsite, and whether you also need written-practice or examination support. Send us the details and we return a quote within one business day.

Is ASNT certification recognised by New Orleans employers?

SNT-TC-1A is the framework most US refinery, chemical, pipeline and fabrication contracts in the region reference. Recognition works through the employer: a client accepts your certification because it trusts the certifying employer's written practice and records. Some offshore or international contracts also name ISO 9712 or other schemes; we do not train to those.

Does my certification move with me if I change contractors?

Not automatically. SNT-TC-1A certification belongs to the employer. A new employer can accept your documented training and experience, but it examines and certifies you under its own written practice.

Which method should I start with to work the river refineries?

UT (thickness first, then angle beam) and VT are the most common starting points for refinery work, with RT if you are joining a radiography crew. For yard and offshore fabrication work, MT and VT come first.

Can you train a whole crew before a turnaround?

Yes. Send us the turnaround date and the certifications needed at the gate, and we plan theory, practical blocks and examinations backwards from that date.

Do you teach LDEQ radiation safety?

No. Our RT course covers technique and interpretation under SNT-TC-1A. Radiation-safety training and the state radiographer examination follow Louisiana's own requirements, and your radiation safety officer arranges them.

Can I practise at home before the practical exam?

You can rehearse setups and scanning logic in the Practical NDT simulator, but your practical exam will be on real specimens and equipment, and experience hours must come from actual work.

Do you offer Level III preparation for New Orleans technicians?

Yes, live online preparation for the ASNT Basic and Method examinations, plus procedure-writing practice. See Level III training and the full training catalogue.
